newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Satellite Broadcasting to reduce capital.
newsitem.headline: Japan Satellite Broadcasting to reduce capital.

text.p: Japan Satellite Broadcasting Inc said on Friday that it hopes to reduce its capital to a 10th of the current 41.6 billion yen by the end of March 1997 in order to realise its aim of listing its shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange by around 2000.

The company, an operator of satellite broadcasting channel WOWOW, will be able to write off part of its accumulated losses of 78.1 billion yen and post an extraordinary profit of 37 billion yen by using part of the value of its shareholders' stakes, a company spokesman said.
In the process, the value of shareholders' stakes would be reduced by 90 percent.
The company's 258 shareholders include Tokyu Corp and Mitsubishi Corp 8058 T.
The company also hopes to start paying a dividend from the 2000/01 business year, he said.
Companies seeking to list their shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange are required to have been posting profits and paying dividends before being considered for a listing.
"We aim to go public by around 2000," the spokesman said.
The company began operating satellite broadcasting channel WOWOW in 1991, but it took until the 1995/96 business year to make an operational profit.
The company expects to post sales of 60 billion yen and parent current profit of 8.5 billion yen in the current 1996/97 business year ending on March 30.
